summary.text:
The best-insulated book in the batch, and the one with the most live optionality. Tameside holds £126.269m against a total CFR of £264.733m, of which £79.620m is PFI and leases, so £58.844m is internal. 93.13% of fixed-rate borrowing matures in ten years or more and nothing at all falls due inside twelve months. The PWLB book costs 3.88% over an average 30 years.

What is interesting is what they did with the discount. In December 2025 they repaid a £10m Barclays loan early and captured about £2.8m on the principal, with Arlingclose analysis behind it. Paragraph 5.7 records that some PWLB loans are now in or close to a discount position too. Whether that is worth acting on depends on the replacement cost, which the report says plainly and does not pretend to settle.

The live item is the LOBOs. £30m remains, with semi-annual call options, and Dexia has already called its £5m at the 16 June 2026 option date — the S151 elected to prepay in full. Each remaining call is a decision that has to be taken against the market on the day, and the Q1 2026/27 report will be the first place it appears.

officer.subject: Your PWLB discount position, priced daily
officer.body:
Hi Jagroop,

Apologies for the cold email. PWLBtoday is fairly new so you may not have come across us yet.

We're built for local authority treasury teams and nothing else: live PWLB rates at both daily fixings, a monthly breakdown of every loan the sector draws, every council's PWLB book priced daily against the DMO's repayment curve, and a training academy for officers and members. There's more — the predictor, the SONIA path, peer metrics, a daily brief — in the brochure at [BROCHURE URL]. We don't sell treasury products, and the data side is free and stays free.

To keep that data and our training relevant we built tools that watch committee papers across every council in the country, so we can see how a council's own figures compare with where the market has gone since. So below are a few thoughts ahead of Audit Committee on 22 September. You're not being singled out — every authority gets one of these — and there's no agenda in it.

A cross-check first: we hold all 18 of your PWLB loans, £96.03m at a weighted 3.88%, which is your Table 2 exactly.

Tameside has the least near-term refinancing exposure of the eight councils we read this month. Nothing matures inside twelve months, 93.13% of fixed-rate borrowing runs ten years or more, and the PWLB half costs 3.88% over an average thirty years — on our side £89.5m of it sits beyond twenty-five years. Against ten-year certainty money at 5.83% today, that's a portfolio doing its job.

What caught our eye was the Barclays repayment. Taking a c. £2.8m discount on a £10m principal in December is the sort of thing that usually only shows up in a footnote, and paragraph 5.7 then notes some PWLB loans are now in or close to a discount position too. That second observation is exactly what we compute, daily, for every council's book against the DMO's premature repayment curve — same formula, banker's rounding, D+1 day count, the lot — so the discount position is a page you look at rather than a piece of work you commission. Yours is at pwlbtoday.org/loan-analysis. We don't present it as a quote; the DMO's is the binding one. But it does mean the question of whether anything has moved into discount is answerable on any given morning, and the answer changes with the curve.

The live item is the LOBOs. Dexia calling the £5m at the 16 June option date, and the S151 electing to prepay, leaves £25m still running with semi-annual options. Each of those is a decision taken against the market on the day rather than at the next report, and with ten-year certainty money at 5.83% and twenty-year at 6.38% the replacement side of it isn't static either. Our monthly sector breakdown at pwlbtoday.org/pwlb-activity is the other half of that picture — July was £368m across 33 loans from just 19 borrowers at an average 5.02%, so you can see how much appetite there is before you need it.

On training, three fit Tameside: LOBO loans, for the £25m still carrying options; Break costs and premature repayment, given where paragraph 5.7 leaves things; and our liability benchmark pathway, which is interactive and built on live data — your own benchmark shows no borrowing need today, which is exactly the position where the indicator earns its keep, and it's worth a look given where CIPFA is heading with the Prudential and Treasury Codes. For members, Audit Committee Chair (Treasury) is written for exactly the committee this report goes to. All 115 courses are free to local authorities until the end of September at pwlbtoday.org/academy, and free accounts for the whole team.

And if you do find it useful, mentioning it to others would help us more than anything. We're small, word of mouth is most of our marketing, and every sign-up helps us prove the need.

Sign up free → https://pwlbtoday.org/
Follow on LinkedIn → https://www.linkedin.com/company/pwlbtoday/

Russell
https://www.linkedin.com/in/russelltew

Source: Treasury Management Outturn 2025/26, Audit Committee, 23 June 2026 (Executive Cabinet, 24 June 2026, Appendix 4).
